transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-15 | Time: 14:00 PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex, Priya, Samira, Ethan (partial), Maya

Summary: quick weekly triage across IT, Finance ops and Security; focus on KMS rotation, SOC 2 evidence, cost allocation tagging, vendor MSAs, and VPC/Private deployment notes.

00:00 Alex: alright let's get started, um, thanks for joining on short notice, I think we have 45 minutes. Priya, Samira, Maya -- I think we have a short agenda, KMS rotation, SOC 2 artifacts, billing tagging gaps, and vendor procurement updates.
00:18 Priya: thanks Alex, yeah I can go first on finance - we've been seeing a couple of unexpected charges in the Dedicated clusters, cost center tagging isn't consistent across projects, so my team is reconciling. I have a draft allocation sheet but there are missing resource tags for about 12 instances.
00:38 Samira: okay that matches the security side where we also saw some VPCs that weren't in the approved inventory. Need those inventoried for the SOC stuff.
00:50 Alex: right; that’s probably from last quarter's burst capacity testing. Maya, any updates on the vendor MSAs that relate to our private deploy package? We had redlines back from the vendor last week.
01:03 Maya: yeah, I pinged them; they did send an updated MSA but legal flagged a couple of indemnity and data residency bits. Ethan, did you get a chance to look?
01:12 Ethan: I skimmed the redlines, mostly standard, a couple of worrying clauses around subprocessor disclosure. I'll need procurement to push for more specific KMS/HSM guarantees and audit rights.
01:25 Samira: audit rights is critical - we need explicit language for access to vendor logs and cryptographic material handling; otherwise SOC auditor will mark as a gap.
01:36 Priya: from billing perspective, if we can't pin these costs to the right projects next month, it will skew our monthly burn reports. I need tagging fixes by next Wednesday ideally.
01:48 Alex: ok, tagging owner - Priya will send the spreadsheet and we'll assign owners. For the infra side, I will run a script to list VPCs and subnets and push to the inventory; but I want to coordinate with Samira so we don't miss private endpoints.
02:01 Samira: yes please, and note that some services are using our internal KMS key for test clusters - we need a rotation plan and documentation of key usage.
02:12 Alex: agreed. I have a proposed key rotation cadence in the runbook but it's not fully up to date for our multi-tenant Dedicated environment and on-prem options. I'll update the runbook to call out the HSM and KMS responsibilities and share by next Monday.
02:26 Priya: also a quick question - are we charging Dedicated cluster reserved capacity to central infra or passing it to business units? Last quarter we split but there was pushback.
02:37 Alex: current policy is central infra until the BU requests direct billing. But we should make that explicit in the allocation doc.
02:45 Priya: cool.
02:48 Samira: on SOC 2 evidence - auditor asked for e.g., key rotation logs, access reviews, and SSO/SAML configs for Okta. We still have a pending item where a couple of service accounts lack MFA on dev clusters.
03:03 Alex: hmm service accounts without MFA - that sounds like a credential management gap. Are those human accounts or machine principals?
03:11 Samira: machines, mostly CI/CD runners created before we enforced the new Okta token exchange. We should add them to the inventory and rotate credentials.
03:19 Alex: I'll add a task to the runbook to automate rotation for service principals and update the CI templates.
03:27 Priya: related to procurement - Maya, can you confirm the billing cycle and any early termination fees on the vendor MSA? That impacts our budget forecast.
03:36 Maya: vendor replied; they have a 60-day notice and a 3 month minimum for reserved capacity; also there are accelerated payment terms for enterprise onboarding. I'll circulate details.
03:45 Ethan: legal will need to review the accelerated payment and make sure our payment milestones are aligned with delivery and SLA. We don't want to prepay and then have misconfiguration problems.
03:55 Samira: SLA aside, we also need to validate their incident response times for security events and escalation paths. The MSA had an ambiguity on 24x7 vs business hours support.
04:07 Alex: okay, action - Maya to push for clear 24x7 incident response in the MSA and Samira to provide required security SLA wording.
04:18 Priya: shifting back to tagging - I've noticed three clusters tagged under legacy project names, and the billing export maps to old GL codes. I'll map those and propose a reallocation.
04:31 Alex: good catch. Also we should centralize the tagging policy repo and give infra service accounts permission to enforce tags at creation time (tagging-as-code). I'll put a PR in the infra repo.
04:42 Samira: for SOC 2 evidence upload - where are we storing artifacts? Currently we have them in the shared drive and some in the audit S3 bucket. We need a single source of truth.
04:54 Priya: why don't we use the audit S3 bucket as canonical and then share read-only links with the auditor; that way we have object versioning and can show MD5s.
05:03 Samira: yes but ensure the S3 bucket is in our compliance account and has encryption with customer-managed CMKs.
05:11 Alex: I'll confirm encryption settings and ensure cross-account access is logged.
05:18 Maya: one more procurement note - a smaller vendor we use for monitoring is pushing a price increase. Do we want to renegotiate now or bundle with the bigger MSA?
05:28 Priya: bundle to get leverage if the timelines match, otherwise negotiate individually.
05:34 Alex: timeline-wise we have to finalize vendor MSA by end of month to meet procurement schedule. Let's prioritize that.
05:42 Samira: quick note on private deployments and VPC peering - engineering flagged potential latency spikes when peering to certain cloud regions with dedicated capacity. We should schedule an infra perf deep-dive to evaluate batching and KV cache behavior across peered VPCs.
05:59 Alex: good call. I'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with infra + runtime team. Tentatively week of Feb 22.
06:08 Priya: that deep-dive will also help model the cost impact for finance, since cross-region egress could add to the bill.
06:17 Samira: also include the security implication of route tables and unintended open ports for peered VPCs.
06:23 Alex: noted.
06:25 Ethan: back to MSA redlines - procurement should give a marked-up doc and I'll aim to respond within 48 hours after I get the final redlines.
06:34 Maya: I'll send the vendor's latest MSA and the procurement notes right after this call.
06:40 Alex: excellent. Any other items?
06:43 Priya: just a small ask - can we get a snapshot of current spend by model type (hosted vs dedicated) for the next finance review? That helps with forecasting.
06:53 Alex: I can get that from usage logs and token-level breakdown; it'll take a day to clean up.
06:59 Samira: and I'll cross-reference with access logs to ensure there are no anomalies.
07:04 Alex: great, let's summarize next steps.
07:09 Priya: (summarizes) Priya will send allocation spreadsheet and mapping for legacy GL codes; Priya to enforce tagging by 2026-02-18.
07:18 Samira: Samira to upload SOC 2 evidence checklist and provide required SLA wording; due 2026-02-19.
07:26 Alex: Alex to update KMS rotation runbook and push tagging-as-code PR; due 2026-02-22.
07:33 Maya: Maya to push vendor MSA redlines to vendor and circulate procurement notes; due 2026-02-25.
07:39 Ethan: Ethan to review MSA redlines and respond within 48 hours of receipt.
07:44 Alex: cool; we'll reconvene next Tuesday for a brief check-in and schedule the infra deep-dive for the week of Feb 22. Thanks everyone.
07:54 Meeting ends.
